text.p: Bonds were well-supported by the recent good news about the single currency but players were reluctant to take risks ahead of the long weekend in Portugal, traders said.
The spreads with the 10-year Bono and Bund remained little changed on Wednesday's close.
"The market is pretty immobile...even if we are in an optimistic phase," said one trader. "I think the spreads are going to remain pretty steady until a clearer trend emerges," he added.
Market confidence had been boosted on Wednesday by figures from the European Commission showing that both Portugal and Spain were on track to pass the economic entry tests for the single currency.
Traders noted that the long weekend coincided with a G7 meeting which was a further reason for caution.
